headline: Qwen3.8-27B GPTQ-Int4 on the Intel Arc Pro B70 via vLLM+MTP — the games are the best on the board (all three fully play-tested, 0 JS errors) and speed is strong (~54-60 tok/s decode, 79 tok/s headline), but the server leaks the model's planning text into the visible answer, which broke the fib/json/constraints harness checks. Composite 8.5 (8/8).
facts: Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-Int4 sym G128 + MTP BF16 draft, served by vLLM nightly xpu image in Docker (container b70-qwen38)
card0 vendor 0x8086 bound to xe driver (PCI 0000:0c:00.0) = the serving GPU (ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0, /dev/dri passed to container); card1 vendor 0x10de is the RTX 3080 Ti serving  — NOT used by this run
79.15 tok/s headline (176 tokens incl. planning preamble); decode-only rates across other tests 53.9-60.7 tok/s
0 reasoning tokens reported on every test — the server does not separate thinking; planning text arrives as content
breakout 44,678 tok / delta 90,653 tok / fractal 60,756 tok — inflated because the model wrote an outline doc + full doc + trailing prose per game; the final doc was extracted and play-tested
all 3: painted + animates + responds, 0 JS errors (breakout 1 canvas, delta 2, fractal 3)
code correct when extracted: fib(50)=12586269025 in 4 µs — harness could not execute raw output because planning text preceded it
valid JSON object present at end of response; harness validation failed on the planning preamble

observations.text: This is a NEW stack (vLLM xpu + MTP speculative decoding) and gets its own row, separate from the frozen 2026-10-04 qwen3.8-27b reference row on the old box layout.

The planning-leak is a server/chat-template property, not necessarily the model's fault: the final answers are almost always correct and separable. Where the leak itself destroyed the deliverable (code-only, JSON-only) the score was penalised; where the final answer was clean (constraints, reasoning) it was judged on the answer.
MTP speculative decoding is working: 54-60 tok/s decode on a 27B GPTQ-Int4 is far above the 3080 Ti rows for the same model family.

open: The thinking-leak could likely be fixed with a chat-template/reasoning-parser change on the vLLM server; a re-run with proper thinking separation would probably lift fib/json/constraints materially. Not done — user's server config left untouched.
Game token counts include the model's multi-document output habit; only the final document was render/play-tested.
delta's 90K-token generation took 1680s, close to the 1800s game timeout — a longer outline habit could time out on a re-run.
